title: Edge TLS renegotiation caused upstream timeouts and amplified retries — cross-deploy mitigation and hotfix
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Summary: During a Friday evening deploy we observed recurring 5xx spikes and end-user timeouts across the Hosted API. Root cause analysis indicates a subtle interaction between an updated kernel-level TLS stack on a subset of serving nodes and our edge proxy connection reuse. The kernel change increased occasional TLS renegotiation duration under heavy ephemeral connection churn; downstream proxies responded with request-level timeouts which triggered exponential client SDK retry behaviour. That combination produced short-lived repair storms that caused cascading 5xx errors and higher queue times for other tenants.

Scope/Impact: Intermittent but high-severity customer-visible errors for ~2% of requests originating in us-west-2 over a 45 minute window. Several enterprise customers reported failed inference requests and increased latency. Impact affected Hosted only in the initial window; Dedicated and Private deployments were not hit directly but required coordination for shared SDK guidance and recommended proxy tuning.

Immediate mitigation performed: 
- Deployed an emergency edge-proxy config change to increase TLS handshake/read timeouts from 10s to 20s for affected pools (hotpatch).
- Added an outbound retry cap at the edge: per-tenant retry budget of 2 attempts with exponential backoff and randomized jitter.
- Temporarily disabled kernel-level TLS renegotiation feature flag on the affected serving pool to restore session reuse behavior.
- Issued customer communications to high-touch accounts and created an incident status page with live dashboard link.

Root cause hypothesis and evidence: 
- Correlated spikes in kernel-level soft interrupts and syscall latency with the exact time window of 5xxs (infra traces + perf events).
- Tracing shows clear pattern: initial request -> long TLS handshake/renegotiate -> proxy times out -> SDK retries with default 3 attempts -> amplified concurrent load -> queue saturation -> 5xx.
- Reproduced locally by simulating short-lived connection churn and forcing TLS renegotiation; observed handshake durations up to 3x baseline under load.

Engineering trade-offs and decisions: 
- Short term: Increase timeouts and enforce retry budgets to stabilize customer traffic (chosen to minimize false-negatives and avoid dropping legitimate long-tail requests).
- Medium term: Patch runtime to prefer long-lived TLS sessions and add handshake backpressure controls in the serving runtime kernel path (more invasive, requires validation).
- SDK guidance: update official SDKs to include jittered retries and clear idempotency token guidance; avoid clients assuming strong idempotency for generation endpoints.

Planned fixes and deliverables: 
1) runtime-1.22 patch to improve TLS session reuse and add a handshake-duration metric (owner: infra/serving) — target release: runtime-1.22-2026.03.
2) edge-proxy: permanent retry-controller that enforces per-tenant budgets and global emergency fastpath (owner: edge infra) — PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/12587.
3) SDKs: deterministic jitter/backoff defaults + idempotency header best-practices doc (owner: client-sdk) — PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/442; https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/210.
4) Observability: new grafana panel for handshake_duration, per-tenant retry_count, and edge-circuit-state (owner: observability).
5) Runbook update and postmortem with concrete SLO implications and compensating controls.

Follow-ups / next steps: 
- QA: run a staged canary of runtime-1.22 patch behind traffic shaping; 2 engineers assigned for smoke tests.
- Postmortem: collect kernel perf traces and customer logs, publish RCA by 2026-03-20.
- Cross-team sync: run a 1-hour tabletop with Support, SRE, Client SDK, and Product to review release gating and retry defaults.

Artifacts and links: 
- Incident dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/incident/edge-tls-reneg-2026-03
- Postmortem draft (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RI/ENG-990001+postmortem
- Hotfix PR (edge config): https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-config/pull/3021

Notes for Dedicated/Private customers: recommended proxy tuning and SDK versions detailed in the Confluence doc. Private on-prem packages may need the kernel TLS behavior audit; engineering SME (Maya Chen) to coordinate with accounts and Solutions Engineering.
